# google_storage_control_project_feature_config

A feature configuration manages a Cloud Storage Smart Storage feature, such as Auto Annotate,
for a project. It defines the buckets that the feature applies to and the feature-specific
settings, such as the AI models used to generate annotations for objects.

~> **Warning:** This resource is in beta, and should be used with the terraform-provider-google-beta provider.
See [Provider Versions](../guides/provider_versions.html.markdown) for more details on beta resources.

## Example Usage - Storage Control Project Feature Config Basic


```hcl
resource "google_storage_control_project_feature_config" "example" {
  provider          = google-beta
  feature_config_id = "feature-config"

  auto_annotate_config {
    models {
      name = "object-detector"
    }
    processing_location = "us"
  }
}
```

## Example Usage - Storage Control Project Feature Config Full


```hcl
resource "google_storage_bucket" "bucket" {
  provider                    = google-beta
  name                        = "bucket"
  location                    = "US"
  uniform_bucket_level_access = true
  force_destroy               = true
}

resource "google_storage_control_project_feature_config" "example" {
  provider          = google-beta
  feature_config_id = "feature-config"
  description       = "Annotates images in a single bucket"

  filter {
    included_cloud_storage_buckets {
      bucket_id_regexes = [google_storage_bucket.bucket.name]
    }
  }

  auto_annotate_config {
    models {
      name = "object-detector"
    }
    models {
      name = "label-detector"
    }
    processing_location = "us"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `auto_annotate_config` -
  (Required)
  The configuration for the Auto Annotate feature, which uses AI models to generate
  annotations for objects in Cloud Storage buckets.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_auto_annotate_config).

* `feature_config_id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the feature configuration, which becomes the final component of its resource name.
  The ID must be 1 to 63 characters long, start with a lowercase letter, and contain only
  lowercase letters, digits, and dashes. The last character can't be a dash.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  A description of the feature configuration. The description can be up to 256 characters long.

* `filter` -
  (Optional)
  A filter that limits the feature configuration to specific Cloud Storage buckets.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_filter).

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.


<a name="nested_auto_annotate_config"></a>The `auto_annotate_config` block supports:

* `models` -
  (Required)
  The list of unique models used to generate annotations. Each model is identified by
  its `name`.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_auto_annotate_config_models).

* `processing_location` -
  (Required)
  The geographic location (case-sensitive) where data is processed. Currently, only
  multi-region locations such as `us`, `eu`, or `asia` are supported.
  To avoid duplicate billing, configure exactly one processing location for each bucket
  and model combination. If you configure multiple processing locations for the same
  bucket and model across different feature configurations, a separate annotation run is
  triggered in each location, and you're billed for each resulting annotation.


<a name="nested_auto_annotate_config_models"></a>The `models` block supports:

* `name` -
  (Required)
  The name of the model. Supported values include `face-detector`,
  `object-detector`, `label-detector`, and `content-safety`.

<a name="nested_filter"></a>The `filter` block supports:

* `included_cloud_storage_buckets` -
  (Required)
  The buckets to include in the feature configuration.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_filter_included_cloud_storage_buckets).


<a name="nested_filter_included_cloud_storage_buckets"></a>The `included_cloud_storage_buckets` block supports:

* `bucket_id_regexes` -
  (Required)
  The names of the buckets to include. For Auto Annotate, regex wildcards aren't
  supported, so specify exact bucket names (for example, `my-bucket`). Each bucket
  must already exist in the feature configuration's project. Up to 1,000 buckets can
  be specified.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/global/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}`

* `name` -
  The resource name of the feature configuration, in the format
  `projects/{project}/locations/global/featureConfigs/{feature_config_id}`.

* `create_time` -
  The time at which the feature configuration was created.

* `update_time` -
  The time at which the feature configuration was last updated.

* `type` -
  The type of the feature configuration, for example `AUTO_ANNOTATE`.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


ProjectFeatureConfig can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/global/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{feature_config_id}}`
* `{{feature_config_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import ProjectFeatureConfig using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    featureConfigId = "<-required value->"
    project = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_storage_control_project_feature_config.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import ProjectFeatureConfig using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/global/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}"
  to = google_storage_control_project_feature_config.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), ProjectFeatureConfig can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_storage_control_project_feature_config.default projects/{{project}}/locations/global/featureConfigs/{{feature_config_id}}
$ terraform import google_storage_control_project_feature_config.default {{project}}/{{feature_config_id}}
$ terraform import google_storage_control_project_feature_config.default {{feature_config_id}}
```
